source.title: Convergence Analysis for Learning Orthonormal Deep Linear Neural Networks
source.authors: Zhen Qin; Xu-Wei Tan; Zhi-Hui Zhu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training convergence and how depth and activation relate to convergence speed, bearing on V4. It does not compare initialization schemes or test the benchmark classification-error claim.
record.gate_note: The study trains orthonormal deep linear networks and reports convergence comparisons. The stated experiment uses MNIST, not CIFAR; it reports no training classification-error values. Orthogonal initialization is used but not compared with another initialization.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal initialization and evaluates its Riemannian training method. It does not isolate initialization's effect on speed or trainable depth. Its theorem assumes initialization near a solution; it does not establish that signal-preserving initialization produces that condition. Optimizer, depth and activation comparisons do not test V4 or another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors establish local linear convergence of RGD under a near-solution initialization assumption, with orthonormal constraints on all but one layer and suitable data, loss and learning-rate conditions. They report faster convergence than GD in MNIST experiments and polynomial depth dependence in their theoretical bound. They explicitly leave initialization methods outside their analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Riemannian gradient descent on orthonormal deep linear networks, with one unconstrained layer; experiments use MNIST MLPs and compare GD/RGD rather than testing CIFAR training-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported convergence changes with layer count, activation function, and optimizer (GD versus RGD).

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST MLPs with 4 or 10 layers, the authors report faster convergence for RGD than GD, slower convergence with increasing depth, and slower convergence but better RGD output error with ReLU than linear activation. Hyperparameters are tuned and initialization differs between optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining orthonormal constraints through RGD can improve convergence relative to GD in the tested MNIST MLP configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 guarantees local linear convergence for orthonormal deep linear networks with one unconstrained layer, whitened inputs, an RCG loss, initialization sufficiently close to a solution and prescribed learning rates. The convergence bound deteriorates polynomially with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RGD has a local linear convergence guarantee for a specified class of constrained deep linear networks.

record.problems: The experiments are on MNIST and use orthonormal deep linear or ReLU MLPs, not the CIFAR benchmark settings in the claim. The plotted curves have no numerical values or uncertainty reported in the text. Initialization schemes are not compared.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported training runs omitted; Figure 1's plotted values are retained as figure-only rows because the text does not state numerical values.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified initialization recipes.

Whether activation-matched, signal-preserving initialization improves training speed or trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V4 verdicts. Using orthogonal initialization does not itself test its benefit, and slower convergence with depth does not qualify V4. The row states are cannot_determine with respect to the listed versions, not denials of the reported optimizer comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration effects on classification error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.
Plain versus shortcut convolutional networks, depth-related training error, and normalization removal.
Initialization schemes are not compared; the study does not test Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability limits, catapult behavior, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization and training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report quicker convergence for RGD than GD; the plotted RGD runs use orthogonal initialization (R3, R7). This supports convergence under the tested setup, not a comparison of initialization schemes.
